'''Zhu Lilan''' ({{lang-zh|s=朱丽兰}}; born August 1935) is a Chinese politician who served as [[Ministry of Science and Technology (China)|minister of science and technology]] from 1998 to 2001 and chairperson of the [[National People's Congress Education, Science, Culture and Public Health Committee]] from 2003 to 2008.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://finance.sina.com.cn/hy/20091204/15217058188.shtml |script-title=zh:图文：全国人大常委、前科技部部长朱丽兰 |work=sina |date=4 December 2009 |access-date=11 July 2022 |language=zh}}</ref>

Zhu was an alternate member of the [[14th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party]] and a member of the [[15th Central Committee of the Chinese Communist Party]].<ref name="celery"/> She was a member of the Standing Committee of the [[9th National People's Congress|9th]] and [[10th National People's Congress]].<ref name="celery"/>

==Biography==
Zhu was born in [[Shanghai]] in August 1935, while her [[Ancestral home (Chinese)|ancestral home]] in Wuxing County (now [[Huzhou]]), [[Zhejiang]].<ref name="celery">{{cite news|url=http://news.sohu.com/20060215/n241845578.shtml |script-title=zh:简历：全国人大常务委员会委员朱丽兰 |work=Sohu |date=15 February 2006 |access-date=11 July 2022 |language=zh}}</ref> After graduating from [[McTyeire School]] in 1955, she was sent to study at [[Odessa University]] on government scholarships.<ref name="celery"/> She returned to China in 1961 and successively served as research team leader, deputy director of the office, deputy research director, associate researcher, and director of the Institute of Chemistry, [[Chinese Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="celery"/> She was a visiting scholar at the [[University of Freiburg]] from 1979 to 1980.<ref name="celery"/>

Zhu joined the [[Chinese Communist Party]] (CCP) in July 1956, and got involved in politics in 1986, when she was appointed executive deputy director of the [[Ministry of Science and Technology (China)|National Technical Committee]].<ref name="celery"/> During his term in office, she headed the [[863 Program]], a program funded and administered by the government of the [[People's Republic of China]] intended to stimulate the development of advanced technologies in a wide range of fields for the purpose of rendering China independent of financial obligations for foreign technologies.<ref>{{cite book| first1= Hequan| last1 = Wu| title = WCC 2000 - ICCT 2000. 2000 International Conference on Communication Technology Proceedings (Cat. No.00EX420)| chapter = The progress of communication technology subject of hi-tech research development plan of China| author-link1=Wu Hequan| volume = 1| date = 2002-08-06| location = [[Beijing]] | isbn = 0-7803-6394-9| pages = 3–4 | doi = 10.1109/ICCT.2000.889157| s2cid = 60832883}}</ref> In March 1998, she was promoted to become [[Minister of Science and Technology (China)|minister of science and technology]], a position she held until February 2001.<ref name="celery"/> In February 2001, she became deputy chairperson of the [[National People's Congress Education, Science, Culture and Public Health Committee]], rising to chairperson in March 2008.<ref name="celery"/>

==Honours and awards==
* August 1997 Fellow of the International Eurasian Academy of Sciences<ref name="celery"/>
